_comment: Species definitions. Base stats and presentation only; a live creature's current HP and energy belong to a pal_instance, never here (TECHNICAL_START.md, Pal Data vs Pal Instance). M11 replaces `model` and the colours with real rigged creatures without touching combat code.
_placeholder: M2 ships coloured capsules on purpose. CLAUDE.md forbids judging creature appeal on placeholders, so these are shaped for READABILITY at combat distance — clearly different silhouettes and clearly different colours — and nothing else.
_comment_catch: `catch_rate` is the species' base share of the catch formula in scripts/combat/catch_math.gd. Lower is rarer. Every species must declare one; tests/test_catch_math.gd fails the build if any is missing, because a creature that is accidentally trivial to catch is the kind of bug nobody reports.
_comment_aggressive: `aggressive` decides whether a wild pal will start a fight on its own. GAME_DESIGN.md 14 forbids simple proximity starting a fight with a PEACEFUL pal, and the same list allows 'Aggressive pal initiates' — so this flag is the line between those two rules, and it lives in data because it is a property of the creature, not of the code.

placeholder._comment_art: Rigged and animated. The model is measured and fitted to `height` at load by pal_body._fit(), so the collider — and therefore the hit cone and the catch accuracy bonus — does not move when the art is swapped. `colour` is retained only for the fallback capsule.
placeholder._comment_animations: Role to clip name. Every pack names its clips differently, so nothing in code knows these strings; a new creature is a data edit. A role a pack lacks falls back (pal_animator._fallbacks) rather than freezing the creature mid-pose.
placeholder._comment_size: Gameplay size, and the art is fitted to it. Raised from the first pass: at a metre the creatures read as small animals underfoot rather than as the things the game is named after, and they were barely legible at combat distance. Combat reach scales off `radius` (combat.json ranges), so these two numbers are tuning, not decoration.

wild_rabbit._comment: The practice creature. Peaceful, common, and generous to catch: it is the one the owner will throw at twenty times while deciding whether throwing is fun, and a rare target would make that a test of patience instead.

wild_bristler._comment: The one that comes at you. Tougher and rarer than the Hopper, because being ambushed should be a moment rather than an interruption — and because the first thing anyone does when something charges them is find out whether they can beat it.
